interactions.label: The video describes four recognisable patterns of surgical hepatobiliary disease

params.question: The video describes four recognisable patterns of surgical hepatobiliary disease. A patient with a slowly enlarging, smooth, rounded liver mass discovered incidentally on imaging, and a history of close contact with sheep, most likely fits which pattern?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Liver abscess presents with fever, right upper quadrant pain, and a tender enlarged liver — not as an incidental imaging finding.

answers.text: Incidental or slowly enlarging cystic mass suggesting hydatid disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus) presents as a slowly enlarging cystic mass, often discovered incidentally, in patients with exposure to dogs or livestock.
The biliary spectrum presents with pain, jaundice, or signs of cholangitis — not as an incidental cystic mass on imaging.
Liver trauma presents acutely after blunt abdominal injury with pain and circulatory compromise, not as a slowly enlarging incidental mass.

overallFeedback.feedback: The four patterns are: (1) febrile painful liver (abscess), (2) incidental cystic mass (hydatid or benign tumour), (3) biliary spectrum (colic to cholangitis), and (4) trauma and malignancy. A slow-growing cyst with livestock contact fits pattern 2 — hydatid disease.
Well done! Recognising which clinical pattern a patient fits is the first step before ordering investigations.

params.question: What is the anatomical basis that allows surgeons to resect individual liver segments without compromising blood supply to the remaining liver?

answers.text: The hepatic artery provides collateral flow to adjacent segments after resection

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The hepatic artery supplies the liver, but it is the segmental independence of each pedicle — not collateral flow — that permits safe resection.

answers.text: Each of Couinaud's eight segments has its own portal pedicle and its own venous drainage

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Each segment receives its own branch of the portal vein, hepatic artery, and bile duct, with independent hepatic venous drainage — making it functionally self-contained.

answers.text: The portal vein provides uniform flow to the entire liver without segmental branching

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The portal vein actually branches to individual segments. It is this branching independence, not uniform flow, that enables safe resection.

answers.text: Hepatic veins form anastomoses between segments, allowing venous rerouting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hepatic veins drain segments independently into the inferior vena cava; they do not form significant inter-segmental anastomoses.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each of Couinaud's eight liver segments has its own portal pedicle (portal vein, hepatic artery, and bile duct) and its own venous drainage — this functional independence makes segmental resection safe.
Excellent! Segmental independence is the anatomical foundation of liver resection surgery.

params.question: A 40-year-old patient from a rural area has a well-defined cystic liver lesion with internal septations on ultrasound. Which investigation is most important before considering any invasive procedure on this lesion?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: AFP is indicated when hepatocellular carcinoma is suspected — typically a solid mass in a cirrhotic liver, not a cystic lesion with septations.

answers.text: ERCP to assess for biliary communication with the cyst

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: ERCP is an interventional procedure with real procedural risk, reserved for therapeutic indications. It is not appropriate as a first-line investigation for a cystic liver lesion.

answers.text: Hydatid serology to confirm or exclude Echinococcus infection

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! Any cystic liver lesion in a patient from an endemic rural area must be evaluated for hydatid disease. Rupture of a hydatid cyst risks releasing scolices that can seed new cysts throughout the abdomen.

answers.text: Contrast-enhanced CT to determine the Couinaud segment involved

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CT provides useful staging and anatomical detail, but confirming or excluding hydatid disease with serology takes priority before any invasive approach.

overallFeedback.feedback: A cystic liver lesion with septations in a rural patient raises strong suspicion for hydatid disease. Hydatid serology is the key investigation before any invasive step — rupture risks peritoneal dissemination of scolices.
Well done! Always confirm or exclude hydatid disease before intervening on a cystic liver lesion — the consequences of unplanned rupture can be catastrophic.

params.question: Amoebic liver abscess requires percutaneous drainage as the primary treatment, similar to pyogenic liver abscess.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Amoebic liver abscess responds to metronidazole alone in most cases and does not routinely need drainage. By contrast, pyogenic abscess requires antibiotics plus drainage plus treatment of the underlying source. This distinction is why amoebic abscess is classified as a medical, not surgical, disease.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct! Amoebic liver abscess is a medical disease treated with metronidazole followed by a luminal amoebicide to clear intestinal carriage. Aspiration is reserved for large, refractory, or rupture-threatening abscesses — unlike pyogenic abscess, which requires antibiotics, drainage, and source control.
